analysis.title: Fed on hold despite strong inflation and accelerating activity
key_insights: The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 3.45%-4% in a 10-2 vote, as widely expected. Both dissenters favoured a 25bp hike.

The press release was more hawkish, acknowledging strong economic activity and high inflation. Most members prefer a more gradual approach and the Fed needs more information on how to bring inflation back to target.
Chair Warsh said inflation remains too high and the Fed has yet to deliver price stability, although he sees encouraging progress. Core inflation is still above 3%.

Warsh expects Q3 GDP growth above 3% annualised, suggesting tighter policy need not derail growth. He stopped short of calling credit conditions tight but acknowledged they have tightened for some households and businesses.

Generali expects two more hikes, one in December and one in Q1 2027 (most likely March), because core inflation is persistent, growth is solid and credit conditions are not yet tight enough to curb inflation.

Structural change: the Fed keeps eight meetings a year but from autumn 2027 one will focus on strategy and may not include a rate decision or statement. By 2028 two will be strategy meetings, leaving six policy-setting meetings, which may pave the way for fewer policy meetings overall.

Generali sees core PCE ending the year around 3% and no sign of labour market weakening. It expects more substantial disinflation in early 2027, which should quickly reduce the need for further tightening.

Market reaction was muted. The S&P rose 0.1% after the announcement and Treasury yields changed little. The curve steepened slightly as the two-year yield fell 5bps after Warsh suggested tightening was beginning to work.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates held, with two of twelve voters dissenting in favour of a 25bp hike, so the committee leans toward tightening.
Core inflation remains above the Fed's target, which supports further tightening.
Warsh's expectation. Strong growth suggests tighter policy need not derail the economy.
Generali does not expect it to ease soon, which supports its two-hike call.

macro_indicators.reading: Two hikes: December 2026 and Q1 2027 (likely March)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Generali's forecast of further tightening before disinflation progresses in early 2027.

risk_factors: Persistent core inflation and solid growth could require more tightening than the market expects.
Credit conditions are not yet tight enough to curb inflation.
A more gradualist committee majority may delay the hikes Generali expects.

tension_points.bull_case: Generali expects two more hikes, in December and Q1 2027, because core PCE stays near 3%, the labour market shows no weakness and credit conditions are not tight enough to curb inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Most FOMC members prefer a gradualist approach and need more information before deciding how to bring inflation down. Warsh suggested tightening is already beginning to work, and Generali expects substantial disinflation in early 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More substantial disinflation in the first months of 2027 would quickly reduce the need for further tightening.
